haiku-low.q1: They do not differ: both return 401 "Invalid email or password". For an unknown email the server still compares against a dummy bcrypt hash and still counts the failure.
haiku-low.q2: It gets a 429 while locked. The password is not checked, nothing is counted, and the lock is not extended.
haiku-low.q3: The existing session is deleted if the browser sent its cookie. A new token is generated and stored, and the browser receives a new Set-Cookie.
haiku-low.q4: Only the session key (the sid value, 32 random bytes base64url). The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: It stops 12 hours after creation, since created_at is never refreshed. It also stops after 30 minutes idle, but continuous use does not reset the 12-hour limit.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes the session row if one exists, then returns 302 to /login with a Max-Age=0 cookie to clear it.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row by key, then replies 302 to /login and clears the cookie. If the row is missing, it is a no-op with the same reply.
haiku-low.q8: In the sess table in Postgres, not in process memory or Redis. Any app instance looks up the session by its key in Postgres.
haiku-low.q9: In the attempts table, one row per failure with email and failed_at. The server counts that email's rows with failed_at in the last 10 minutes; older rows drop out of the count.
haiku-low.q10: It checks last_seen_at is under 30 minutes old and created_at is under 12 hours old. When valid, it writes last_seen_at as now.
haiku-low.q11: A 503 with no Set-Cookie. The user is not logged in, and the old session has already been deleted.
haiku-low.q12: An hourly cleanup that deletes sess rows idle over 30 minutes or older than 12 hours, plus old attempt rows and expired lock rows. It can run on either or both app boxes.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both get a 401 with the text "Invalid email or password". For an unknown email the server still compares against a dummy bcrypt hash and still counts the failure, so timing and lockout look identical.
sonnet.q2: The lock is in effect (locked_until = now + 15 min in login_locks), so the server returns 429. It doesn't check the password, doesn't count the attempt, and doesn't extend the lock.
sonnet.q3: After a successful password check, the server deletes the old session row (if a cookie was sent). It then issues a fresh token and inserts a new row. The old key is never reused.
sonnet.q4: Only the session key (the sid, 32 random bytes base64url) and no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after creation (created_at more than 12 h ago; cookie Max-Age is also 43200). Activity doesn't extend this, even though the 30 min idle limit is refreshed by the touch.
sonnet.q6: It deletes the session row if one exists and replies 302 to /login with the cookie cleared (Max-Age=0).
sonnet.q7: The server deletes the sess row by key, then replies 302 to /login and clears the cookie. If the row is already missing, the delete is a no-op and the reply is the same. If the DB is down, it returns 503 and doesn't clear the cookie, so a retry works.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres sess table, keyed by the token. Nothing is in process memory and there is no Redis. Either instance looks up the cookie's sid value in that shared table.
sonnet.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failure with email and failed_at. The server counts that email's rows with failed_at in the last 10 minutes. There is no window start or reset, and older rows just fall out of the count.
sonnet.q10: It compares last_seen_at against now (idle no more than 30 min) and created_at against now (age no more than 12 h). When the session is valid, it sets last_seen_at to now (the touch).
sonnet.q11: A 503 with no Set-Cookie. The user isn't logged in, and the old session is already gone.
sonnet.q12: An hourly cleanup job. It deletes sess rows idle more than 30 min or older than 12 h. It can run on either app box or both.
